brightness.note_plain: Horizons predicts V 15.9 to 16.6, brighter than our pipeline's 50% recovery limit, magnitude 17.7 (injection study aquarius-2025w23): it should stand out in these images. Horizons predicts visible-light brightness (V) while SPHEREx sees near-infrared light, so this is a rough comparison.

notes: 38 of 276 predicted positions are interpolated from Horizons' daily geocentric table (not computed from SPHEREx's own position), which can be off by several arcseconds for nearby objects.

response.summary_plain: JPL's predicted position of 495 Eulalia (A902 UL) falls inside 276 SPHEREx frames, in 50 visits from Jan 20, 2026 to Jul 25, 2026 (IRSA's public SPHEREx images run through Jul 25, 2026).
response.why_it_matters_plain: Old images that happen to show a known object are called precovery observations. Each one adds a position at a new date, which lengthens the stretch of time over which 495 Eulalia (A902 UL) has been observed. A longer observed arc pins down the orbit, so future positions can be predicted more precisely. The frames below are where SPHEREx's images should contain 495 Eulalia (A902 UL), according to JPL's current orbit.
